walkthroughs.body_html:
An Introduction to Philosophy of Religion — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

An Introduction to Philosophy of Religion brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with An Introduction to Philosophy of Religion.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Rerum Novarum
Pacem in Terris
Laudato Si

mcqs.q: What is the maximum number of wives in Islam?
What is the relationship between atman and Brahman in Hindu philosophy?
options: Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.

Atman is the individual self/soul; Brahman is ultimate reality. In Advaita Vedanta, atman IS Brahman — the self is identical with ultimate reality, and liberation comes from realising this non-duality.
Atman is the body and Brahman is the soul.
Atman and Brahman are two competing Hindu gods.

mcqs.q: What does utilitarianism say is right action?
options: The action that produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number — judged by consequences, not intentions or rules.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
Whatever makes you personally happy is the right thing to do.
Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.

mcqs.q: What does natural law theory base morality on?
options: Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.
Natural law means whatever happens in nature is morally right.
Atman and Brahman are two competing Hindu gods.
Human nature and reason — there are objective purposes (telos) built into humans which reason can discover, generating universal moral precepts.
